headline: A Democratic candidate for Congress in Wisconsin has threatened legal action against her Republican opponent over AI-made videos that show her saying things she never said.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 5: the letter was sent 30 Sep 2026 (before 2 Oct), no lawsuit has been reported, and the Axios original could not be read.
importance_line: Voters in the Wisconsin race and anyone shown in fake campaign videos are affected, and it tests whether older defamation law can cover AI fakes where election-specific rules are thin; so far it is a warning letter and no lawsuit has been reported.
summary: Wisconsin Public Radio reports that lawyers for Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter on 30 Sep 2026 to Rep. Derrick Van Orden over AI-made videos he posted on X, saying defamation law may apply and that she is weighing "all legal options". A cease-and-desist letter is a warning rather than a lawsuit, and Van Orden's campaign accused Cooke of throwing a "full blow tantrum".
notes: Original outlet Axios (blocked, 403). Written from Wisconsin Public Radio on the Cooke and Van Orden letter; the Axios story may include other legal threats not covered here.
